variants.prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual.
Create ONE single landscape 16:9 pitch slide for a startup named AdaptOps, intended as the sole slide shown on stage. Full slide only, no device mockup, no outside frame. English throughout. High-resolution, crisp text, one refined neo-grotesque font family in normal/medium/bold weights. Clear letterspacing and genuinely comfortable whitespace.
Received brand and tagline MUST be exact:
"AdaptOps"
"Adapt as fast as your market changes."
Supporting sentence:
"An agent that knows your business, prepares a coordinated plan and executes approved actions."

Core product:
The experience opens with a company report ALREADY PREPARED, not a blank chat, watch configuration, or generic monitoring feed. The agent first knows authorized company facts AND prior research; follows sector and regional events; establishes evidence-supported risks, opportunities and mixed effects; prepares one coordinated procurement/operations/sales/finance plan; executes only approved actions within rights; verifies results; preserves knowledge and decisions and revises the plan when facts change. Do not collapse this into just watching news, revealing insights, or emergency purchasing.
Timber/materials is the first market. The company vision applies to inventory/supply-dependent businesses, without claiming proven cross-industry adoption. These are product-vision mockups, not screenshots or proof that the full loop is already built. No real execution receipt, real industrial incident or verified customer link is asserted.
Illustrative synthetic scenario: a supply incident and potential additional local demand. Do not invent prices, customers, counts, savings, manufacturer names or factual relationships.

Visual language:
Premium airy product storytelling, inspired by restrained modern SaaS sites and strong editorial slide design. White and very light neutral backgrounds, charcoal text, deep petrol teal and soft mint accents. Subtle amber for risk. Purposeful well-crafted product UI fragments are allowed and encouraged. The UI should explain prepared intelligence, coordinated action and memory. Do not render a dense analytics dashboard. Absolutely no robots, stock illustrations, 3D factories, neon, network spaghetti, decorative clipart, giant financial metrics or heavy consulting tables. No more than one main application scene or three simple moments. Keep text readable at presentation scale and preserve negative space.
Place a small but unambiguous A, B or C direction badge in the top-right margin. The direction label is not part of the brand. Make the headline/brand and the product scene the two main reading levels. Avoid additional marketing paragraphs.

Required concise content, render verbatim but distribute through the composition rather than repeating:
Main proposed app-view title: "Your company brief is ready"
A small context/source line: "ERP / CRM / WMS + prior research"
Signal text: "Supply incident. Local demand to qualify."
Impact text: "Commitments to protect. Opportunity to assess."
Four coordinated plan lines:
"Procurement: confirm alternative supply"
"Operations: preserve existing deliveries"
"Sales: qualify additional demand"
"Finance: review spend and margin"
One clear human approval/execution control: "Approve & execute"
One continuity line: "Verify results. Save knowledge. Reassess."
Small example label: "Illustrative synthetic scenario"

The bottom or side margin should retain three concise, clearly separated pitch criteria:
"WHO" followed by "Operations and procurement teams. Starting with multi-site timber and materials."
"WHY NOW" followed by "Agents can research, calculate and act through connected tools."
"FIRST USERS" followed by "Planned: founder introductions to French timber/materials design partners."
One small but readable final scope line:
"Product vision. Synthetic demo. Current proof: risk flow on Aiven. Full loop and benchmark pending."

You may use these short section labels where useful: "Company context", "What changed", "Business impact", "Shared plan", "Approved actions", "Results and memory".
Do not add other body text. No invented metrics, numerical proof, integration logos, URLs, QR codes, or brand icons. Keep sample actions in a proposal/approval state; do not mark a real purchase as completed. Include both risk and opportunity visually with equal weight. Do not pretend opportunities or connected-system execution are already proved. No em dash.

COMPOSITION A: THE PREPARED COMPANY BRIEF. Badge A.
Use an asymmetrical editorial split. Left third: AdaptOps wordmark, a strong but elegantly sized multi-line tagline, then the short supporting promise, with substantial whitespace. Right two-thirds: ONE large exquisite product view of the already prepared company brief, not a group of feature cards. Inside that view, start with the exact brief title and context line; use two short callouts for the signal and business impact with evidence marks, then the four cross-functional plan rows as a single shared document. Give the Approve & execute action real visual priority near the lower edge. Put continuity below the action in the same product view, making verification, memory and reassessment clearly downstream. Use a restrained window header but no browser chrome or fake URL. The three pitch criteria form a clean light footer row, outside the product view. An investor should immediately understand that the user receives a ready-to-review response for their own business.
